body:
## Summary

- **Round admission (P-b1, pull):** the capacity gate (#4712) now runs before the first model call (unchanged) **and after every round's tools complete**, via an `AUTO_FUNCTION_INVOCATION` filter + ContextVar controller (`sk_agent_turns.py`). A refusal — or an exhausted `options.max_rounds` budget — **pauses** the turn: `status:"paused"`, `resumable:true`, `round_index`, gate verdict. The pause rides SK's `terminate`: the round in flight always completes (`asyncio.gather` finishes before the terminate check) and everything commits to the thread — **nothing in flight is killed**.
- **`options.continue` (P-a):** resumes a paused epoch on the same `conversation_id` — no new user message, tools already executed never re-run, fresh round budget.
- **Durable conversations (P-a, opt-in `SK_AGENT_CONVERSATION_DIR`):** user/assistant texts + per-turn tool journal survive restarts. A restarted resume replays model calls and answers journaled tool calls from the journal — **idempotent defer, no double execution**. `end_conversation` clears the persisted state.
- **Per-conversation lock (P-a):** a concurrent second turn on one conversation is refused as `conversation_busy` — never interleaved history mutations.
- **Timeout/cancel rollback (P-a):** the pending user message is rolled back under the lock and the error names the `conversation_id` (it did not before).
- **Envelope (P-a):** every `call_agent` response carries `conversation_id`, `turn_index`, `round_index`, `status` (`completed|paused|error`); runtime gate refusals are pauses (resumable), malformed-gate config errors stay errors.
- **`run_conversation` gates + timeout (P-b3):** same pre-dispatch gates as `call_agent` (rate limit per agent, capacity gate per distinct model — refusal before any model call) and a bounded ceiling `options {"timeout": N}` (default 900 s, `0` = unbounded) instead of running unbounded.
- **Gate defect fix:** a probe whose **script is missing** dies inside its interpreter (`python missing.py` exits 2) and was classified `red` ("Swift saturated") when nothing was measured; stderr launcher-failure signatures now reclassify it `unknown` (still refused — fail-closed preserved). Also fixes the container mislabeling deduced in the issue.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_turn_control.py` (23 tests, **real SK loop** — scripted `ChatCompletionClientBase` + counting `@kernel_function` tool, only the network is fake):
  - closure criterion 1: gate pauses between two rounds (probe flipped red from inside round 1's tool), resume with same `conversation_id`, **tool call counter unchanged** (1 across pause + resume);
  - round-budget pause (`max_rounds`), resume completes with fresh budget;
  - **restart** between pause and resume (new manager, empty memory, same store): journal replay answers the re-issued tool call — counter of the new process stays 0, exactly one execution overall;
  - pre-dispatch refusal envelope (paused + conversation_id + zero model calls), completed-turn envelope, option validation;
  - concurrency lock (`conversation_busy`), timeout rollback (pending user message removed, turn index not consumed);
  - closure criterion 2: `run_conversation` refuses on red gate before any model call; `options.timeout` bounds the run; invalid values refused;
  - probe-absent verdict `unknown` (not `red`) + real-red exit stays red; durable store round-trips, journal clear, delete, path confinement.
- [x] Full suite: **926 passed**; the 7 remaining failures are pre-existing environment failures (PDF probes / D:\dev paths), verified identical on the pristine tree (stash + rerun).
- [ ] CI (ubuntu) — expected green; `test_source_file_channel` relative-path failure is Windows-only, passes in CI per ms#1769's observation.

Refs roo-extensions#4742 (closure criteria 1+2 as CI tests; the E2E measure with the live vllm harness remains for the vllm lane, per the issue's own scoping) · #4712 · CoursIA#26534
